steps.text: Mix soy sauce, ketchup, vegetable oil, garlic, salt, pepper, and oregano together in a small bowl.

Score both sides of steak in a diamond cut, about 1/8 inch deep. Rub marinade into both sides of the meat. Store in a covered dish or resealable plastic bag in the refrigerator to marinate for 5 to 6 hours, or overnight. Flip meat every few hours.
Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat, and lightly oil the grate.
Place steak on the preheated grill. Cook for 3 to 7 minutes per side, or to the desired doneness.

raw_recipe.headline: London Broil
raw_recipe.description: This London broil recipe is a quick fix for an inexpensive cut. Mix up a flavorful marinade and let the meat sit overnight for a perfect flank steak.

review.reviewBody:
Excellent recipe! Now, when London Broils are on sale, I buy several, make a big batch of this marinade, let them sit a day or two, then put them in individual freezer ziploc bags, with the marinade. Then, on a busy day, I can just pull out the pre-marinated steaks, defrost, grill, and enjoy! Great time and money saver, and so yummy!

Janelle

I've never made london broil before, and this recipe worked great for me. The only reason I gave it 4 stars was because I added more garlic - I used 3 Tbsp of minced bottled garlic. I think that was perfect. I marinated the meat for almost 24 hours, and since there was snow outside on our grill ;) I broiled the steak in the broiler for approx. 8 min. per side, and sliced very thin. Take the meat out while it still looks a little too rare, because it will keep cooking, and it definitely is better on the rare side. Overall, excellent marinade. Will make again.

Very good marinade with a few additions. I read over a couple of reviews that mentioned the meat didn't come out very tender so I added about 3 Tbls of lemon juice to act as a tenderizer. I also added about 2 tsp of worchestershire sauce..(we call it rooster sauce), 2 tsp of fish sauce, 1 tsp of ground ginger, chili sauce instead of ketchup and a tsp of garlic powder. I broiled this instead of grilling (due to the nasty weather) and it turned out really good. My husband had 2 large peices and my 16 month old (who doesn't have all of her teeth) was able to eat this. Will use again. Thanks Jill.

This was really quick to prep in the morning before work. Added 2 T red wine vinegar on advice of other reviewers to help tenderize the meat (didn't have any lemon juice). Took it out of the fridge an hour before I started cooking. Seared on both sides in cast iron skillet, covered loosely w/ foil, and put in a 400 degree oven for 7 minutes. Let rest 10 min and sliced very thin. I also brought the leftover marinade to a boil and let it thicken, and spread it over the top of the steak while it cooled. Really good, will make again!

Very tasty. Took some hints from other reviews because my London broil cut of meat was thick. Added 2 tblsp of lemon juice to marinade to help tenderize the meat. Allowed meat to marinate for 48 hours. I used a ziplock bag. 
Broiled my meat about 7 to 8 minute
Es per side and then wrapped in aluminum foil and allowed to set for 10 minutes before slicing. I’ve tried London broil many times and was never happy with results. This was the best. Will make again.

This isn't your mother's shoe-leather London Broil done in a pan of water in the oven like my mother used to make when I was a kid! I used to despise eating any meat or roast she would make as it was always so dry and tough. I vowed to never put my family through that ordeal and learned how to cook. I was skeptical about this recipe since the marinade is/was so simple. I am used to adding tons of spices, wine, etc., and rarely stick with a recipe. BUT... this easy-peasy recipe caught my eye. My London Broil turned out phenomenal! I ended up marinating it for 24 hours as I just wasn't able to get back to making it within 5 hours. During that 24 hours of marinating though I did flip it and rubbed it down each time (about 4 times in all). I thought I'd try making it in a skillet on the stovetop. I used very high heat since I have an electric stove (blah). I did the recommended time of 5 minutes per side. It was perfecto! This was a really good deal for just $12 bucks (fed 4) and was a decent quality of meat from my local grocer which is known for the quality of their meats. I will be making this more often.

Thanks Jill. Made it yesterday with Josie's additions. 3 tbls of lemon juice to 2 tsp of Worcestershire sauce, 2 tsp of fish sauce, 1 tsp of ground ginger, chili sauce instead of ketchup and 2 tsp of garlic powder. Cut the four pounds into four one pound servings. Wife and I ate one serving. One serving's in the refrigerator. Two in the freezer. Thanks to all you great cooks. From a beginner.

This is the best tasting London Broil I've ever ate. I doubled the marinade for a 2-lb cut, scored it, and put it all in a doubled zip locked bag. The meat marinated for 48 hours prior to broiling for 8 minutes on each side (medium rare). Delicious.

Delicious! I omitted the ketchup and added lemon juice as someone else stated. I also added some Montreal steak seasoning, onion powder, garlic powder, whorchestire sauce, a little bit of siracha and a splash of red wine vinegar. Stuck it in the sous vide for 6 - 7 he's and it came out super tender! I never thought London broil could be that tender!!! Definitely making this again!

Super easy and flavorful marinade! It was a nasty rainy day outside, so I seared the meat 5mins on each side on the stovetop in a cast iron skillet then finished in the oven. I let a pat of herbed butter melt overtop it while it rested before slicing. Mmm. Will make again!

I made this twice...the first time I followed the recipe exactly as presented and grilled it on my Pit Boss pellet grill using hickory pellets...yummmmm. The next time I made London broil I slightly modified the marinade by adding 1 tbs of red wine vinegar, substituting barbecue sauce for the catsup, and marinated the meat in a sealable freezer bag, adding about 1/2 cup of sliced raw onion. Cooked it the same way and O M G, what a difference! The meat was noticeably more tender and the flavor of the marinade was simply outstanding. Served it with seasoned roasted baby red potatoes and cole slaw and grilled corn on the cob...This is a new family favorite!
We all love it

This was a great marinade, I did make a few tweeks. I added apple cider vinegar for a acid with the ketchup, I saw a bunch of people used lemon juice but I use the vinegar in my BBQ sauce it works well. I also tried it with tomato paste works just as well if you want to use it. I don't have a grill so I went with using the broiler on high for 5 minutes per side, remember to take some crumbled tin foil to prop the oven door open this keeps the broiler from turning off. Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting the meat, you can wait 5 minutes but 10 is better. I made homemade Amish white bread (also from this site) made open faced sandwiches with beef gravy (I cheated and used pre-made jar gravy) and poured it over. Served with mashed potatoes and glazed carrots.
This was delicious, everyone loved it. Definitely a keeper!
We use it to marinade our steaks too! Love it!

I followed the recipe with the exception of adding a 1/2 tsp more of minced garlic. I also sliced some garlic very thin, made horizontal slices in the thickest parts of the meat (on sides) & slid those slices into the meat. I flipped it twice (each time after about 3-4 minutes) & cooked (broiled) to 135° and it was a perfect medium-well! Glad I let it rest for 10 minutes. I have never had such a great tasting London Broil.

I followed Josie's suggestion and added 3 Tbls of lemon juice, 2 tsp of worchestershire sauce, 2 tsp of fish sauce, 1 tsp of ground ginger and chili sauce instead of ketchup and a tsp of garlic powder. I marinated the meat for 24-48 hrs since its a tough piece of meat.
This has been my go-to London Broil marinade for the past 20 years. Love it!
Easy recipe to follow Made my own ketchup and used amino acids vs soy sauce. Needed to marinate longer for a 2 pound slab
Maybe I use Worcestershire sauce next time for more flavor...or a bit of red wine.
